faces.f: "With what sorry scraps of power do you think to oppose me?"
"I will unravel you piece by piece."
"I will make you a monster to haunt your own dreams."

n: Rot Like the Scum You Are

faces.n: Rot Like the Scum You Are
faces.f: "Defy me, and you will dissolve inch by screaming inch."
"Yes, flee from me, prey! Flee from your inevitable fate until your feeble mortal body collapses. I will drink my fill of your fear."
"I can stretch a single moment of agony into centuries."
"Do you not grow tired of your futility? I know I do."
"When you die alone, know that it was I who took everything from you."

n: You Live Only Because I Will It

faces.n: You Live Only Because I Will It
faces.f: "Do not fear death. Fear me."
"Know that the pain you feel now is but an infinitesimal fraction of the agony I will soon inflict upon you."
"Know, as you perish, that all it took was a single misstep for you to fall into my clutches."
"I will craft exquisite tortures from the roiling depths of your terrified mind."
"Cower before your true selves."
"You will crawl through the ashes of your own grand ambitions before I grant you the mercy of death."
The soul of a murderer from the old world, steeped for centuries in rot and malevolence.
As their bodies crumbled to ash, the cultists' terrible smiles only grew wider.
Those who try to rob a grave claimed by a necromancer rarely make the same mistake twice.
"I used to cheat death every day in practice. This is nothing."
"Oh, we don't *need* to operate. I've just always wanted to try it."
Within the silken shroud, all doubts are cleansed, and all desires are united with Valgavoth.
Clad in the light of conviction and hope, Linette strode forth to face Duskmourn's terrors without fear.

"Strictly speaking, you can't kill what's already dead, but trapping and disintegrating it is pretty close."
—Garden, survivor technologist
As it slunk toward her, Nina told her legs to run, but they stayed rooted and rigid. She screamed—but no sound left her lips.
Its unblinking gaze sees every flaw, every shame, every humiliating moment you wish you could forget.
In life, Marcus had been a devoted guide of new arrivals. Death simply made it easier to get around.
"Well, hello there. Want to come exploring?"
"It's not magic. I read the writing on the House's walls. I listen to its sighs. I smell the changes in its air. It tells me where danger lies."
"Boo!"
The survivors would no longer be picked off one by one. It was their turn to hunt.
"A void rod? Perfect! Now I'll be able to get the glitch reader working again."
Their only family is each other, and their only toys are those who wander too far into the fields.
When it ripped, its owner attempted to fix it. Something went... wrong.
When their would-be sacrifice wandered back to their encampment, the survivors breathed a sigh of relief, assuming the demon had departed.
"You're safe, kiddo! For at least the next ten minutes. That's about all I can promise."
Tyson tried to scream for help, but his lungs simply unraveled.
With a flick of their wrist, Niko shattered the wickerfolk and whisked Nashi to safety.
"This way, Melinda. A hundred years haven't improved your sense of direction."

"Don't be a wimp. We'll cover more ground this way."
—Rian, former survivor
Those who mock its ragged surface and seeping eyes have a curious tendency to go missing.
"Sure, I'm pretty small, but Gribble isn't, so I don't get scared."
Maggie had always wanted to be on television.
"Come play with us."
Sometimes, survivors in the Floodpits hear their own drowning voices crying out for help. Only the ones who flee immediately live to speak of it.

"Be on your guard. Valgavoth has eyes everywhere. And I don't mean that figuratively."
—Winter
Valgavoth's evil aura turned the shark from an apex predator into an inescapable terror of the deeps.
Jace kept his mouth shut, but he couldn't shake the feeling that the strange creatures could hear the screaming in his mind.
All who enter the House hear Valgavoth's whispers, worming through their consciousness until they can no longer resist his influence.
Though she was used to stepping into the unknown, something about this strange doorway made the Wanderer shiver as she crossed the threshold.
"The readings are off the charts! Whatever it is, it's close."

"What's got you all bent out of shape?"
—Joseph, comedian, last words

"W-wait! What do you mean this quiz determines half our grade?"
—Zimone, muttering in her sleep
It had been months since Jakob had started falling but only a few weeks since he'd run out of breath to scream.
On the second day after he'd been separated from his friends, Tino worried they'd be panicking at his absence. By the fourth, he was certain they'd never cared for him at all.
Kaito's blade brought the light of another plane into Duskmourn, and with it, a brief chance to escape.
Once charged with watching over every room in the original Vendrell house, it doggedly surveys the endless, ever-expanding labyrinth.
At first Sasha felt silly fending off the cellarspawn hordes with the essence of her childhood pet hamster. But it sure beat dying alone in the dark.
It slices away the most precious memories first, then the mundane, until all that remains is blank, formless fear.
"If I've done this right, it should immobilize all spirits in the area. If I've done this wrong... you know what, let's just hope I did it right."
They thirst for blood like mosquitoes do. They just have a less dainty way of accessing it.
With sandy beaches in short supply, Duskmourn's crabs have adapted to burrow into everything from carpet to flesh.
"Just a shadow. It's only a shadow. Please let it be a shadow."

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after IV.)
I, II, III — Mill two cards. If two cards that share a card type were milled this way, draw a card and repeat this process.
IV — Exile any number of target instant, sorcery, and/or Tamiyo planeswalker cards from your graveyard. Copy them. You may cast any number of the copies.

faces.f: Though he needed to know what lay beyond the intersection, Harp couldn't suppress a shiver of disquiet as his glimmer disappeared into the darkness ahead.
The Wanderer flung out her hand, but too late—Kaito had vanished into the House's maw.
It moves with the speed of a spider but none of its skittering grace, scuttling to the sound of mucus-covered fingers.
Adapted to feed on dead flesh, it's not averse to making its own when no corpses are available.
Every death was funnier than the last, until his howling laughter drowned out his victims' screams.

"See?! That's why you always burn the bodies."
—Rip, spawn hunter
Elsa swelled with euphoria and power as she stepped over her friends' corpses. She should have bargained with a demon a lot sooner.
Ears ringing and head throbbing, all Tarvin could do was wait to see what would finish the job.
"Thanks, but no thanks. I'm done with hope."
"There are worse things here than vampires."
Valgavoth whispered into Marina's ear until he was all she could hear.
"All stars grow dark. All worlds come to an end."
"Valgavoth wants our pain, our terror! We cannot join him unless we suffer!"
As it drew closer, Sam felt her own teeth wriggle in their sockets, as if they wanted to leap out and join the thing.
The first thing it kills is the light.
The cries of survivor and cellarspawn mingled in a single, terrible roar as they plunged into the fathomless depths.

"Come. Strip yourself of flesh and fear. Hunt for me. *Entertain* me."
—The Lord of Pain
Vicky was so tired. The pain began to fade. "You were so brave," said her grandmother's voice from somewhere far away. "But it's time to rest now."
Cracks in the facade of the House lead not to escape but to oblivion.

"I grant them the illusion of hope so that their despair grows ever sweeter."
—Valgavoth
"Hush, little ants. I can rid you of your troubles with a breath. All I ask in return is a drop of blood... and a promise."
Razorkin have only one hobby.
"I know you'd want me to live, bestie!"

"That's the one good thing about these cultists: sometimes they do your work for you."
—Winter
"Can we trust him?" Niko whispered as they eyed the stranger. "I don't know," the Wanderer replied, "but he's a lot friendlier than the creature that was chasing us."
Each spindrell is the lingering consciousness of a survivor consumed by cellarspawn—a ragged, drifting remnant pulsing with constant psychic agony.
It had heard monsters were supposed to hide under beds, and it did its best.

"This is my way out. You'll have to find your own."
—Winter, to Niko
"Go ahead, meat. Run."
Dance to its beat, or it will dance on your grave.
"Hey! Fang-faces! Over here!"
It makes no effort to hide itself, savoring its prey's rising panic as the sound of its clacking skull grows closer and closer.
Unfortunately, the keyhole turned out to be located in an even larger, scarier clown mouth.
In the darkness, Lana reached for Shay's hand and squeezed it for comfort. Then she heard Shay call to her from the next room.
No living being, survivor or monster, is exempt from Valgavoth's wrath.
Torain had never lost a match in his life, and he didn't plan to start now.
"I don't know what it was! Why would I stick around to find out?"
"Remember when you smashed me for a little pocket money?"

"In my younger days, I would meticulously catalog all the terrors I encountered. These days, I mostly just kill them with fire."
—Rip, spawn hunter
"You tried to throw me away, Henry. I don't like that at all."
The souls of those who perished before Valgavoth's Ascension exist now only as fractured echoes of who they once were.
"Know your place, pets! First blood is mine!"
"Stitch your eyes, stitch your skin, stitch your mouth into a grin."
"Listen to that tasty squelch. Good hit, good hit! Come here now, little meatbag!"
Kaito ran. Illusion or no, the fire felt hot enough to kill.
She sees the faces of those who wronged her in everyone she encounters.
All it took to shatter their lifelong bond was a scrap of hope.
"Scared, are you? Need a hug?"
"No! This worked perfectly in the lab!"
As the ghost clawed its way into her skin, Sarissa forgot that the rage tearing through her heart wasn't her own.
"Surprise! Aaahahahahah! You should see the look on your face. Here, let's peel it off so you can!"
Rage can be a potent antidote to fear.
The melody was all in her head, but she'd always preferred to dance alone.
The touch of its many hands is almost gentle, at first. But then the grip tightens, and the mandibles dig in.
No one knows what hides beneath the beasties' masks.
"We got more than most people do. We got the chance to say goodbye."
She came back alone, with her recorder broken and its footage scrambled. Whatever she had experienced, she never spoke of again.

Zimone's theory was that the fractalization of atmospheric aether would increase kinetic energy. Tyvar's theory was that if you hit cultists in the face really hard, they would fall down. They were both right.
"Please be dead, please be dead, please be dead."
"The dark should be scared of me!"
A mouth like that can never keep secrets.
Symptoms of a burrower bite include fevers, chills, gangrene, subcutaneous writhing, a growing urge to eat the flesh of the living, and if you're lucky, death.
With his friends dead and his weapons broken, Taros seized the only thing he could to defend himself.

"We ran, but it was all around us—like a writhing, flailing forest of rubbery limbs and stabbing talons."
—Survivor's journal

"We set it on fire. It lived. We cut off its head. It lived. We fell to it, one by one. It lives."
—Sunrise, survivor sentry
Wherever it grows, wood rots, walls turn gray, and flesh becomes fertilizer.
She's got a heart of gold, a nose for danger, and jaws that can pulverize a cellarspawn with a single snap.
Life thrives in the Hauntwoods, but it follows its own laws, unbound from the natural order.

"That's why I never travel without a flamethrower."
—Rip, spawn hunter
Even as the roots twisted painfully into his flesh, he sang out in joy, for he could feel himself becoming one with the woods.
It doesn't know it isn't real.

"Hey, look! It made us a nice big path through the hedge maze!"
—Zimone
"They just keep coming and coming—perfect for my morning workout!"
Tyvar and the Wanderer were done running.
Valgavoth harbors a special loathing for dogs, whose mere presence provides a powerful antidote to the fear he craves.
Every night, Cori threw the unsettling doll away. Every morning, it was back on the shelf, its eyes following her every move.

"Valgavoth commands us to feed the trees. Let our blood be their mulch, our flesh their soil."
—Victor, Valgavoth's seneschal
There are some nightmares so terrible, you're never truly rid of them.
"Do they cause trouble? Sure. But if you're nice to them, the trouble happens to other folks."
Glimmers are physical manifestations of survivors' hope and courage. Their presence is one of the few things that can protect from Valgavoth's malevolent influence.
The souls of those who perished outside the House persist as fractured echoes, driven to share their misery with the living.

"They might look funny, but when all those teeth sink into your flesh, you won't be laughing."
—Winter
"Huh, the detector won't stop beeping. Must be on the fritz again."
Those who glimpse the House's true nature firsthand are cursed to never again look away.
All his tales are cautionary.

"At least the razorkin are happy when they kill you. The walkers don't even notice."
—Angus, survivor scout
Farley had always been the fastest on the track team. But no one was cheering anymore.

"Isn't fire supposed to *kill* those things?"
—Tyvar
Pop goes the evil.
Every time its teeth tasted blood, its hunger grew, until one day it was no longer a trap but a hunter.
Best friends are great to share secrets with—like where the matches are, or how to find a human heart.
Hope and reliable lighting are in short supply in the House. Glimmers provide both.
If you find them, they wanted to be found.

"If you see a light moving toward you in the darkness, don't assume it's coming to help."
—Winter
In a moment of bloodthirsty whimsy, a razorkin once picked up a ventriloquist's puppet and used it to terrorize a survivor. Now it hunts on its own, with no one pulling its strings.
They say every inhabitant vanished in a single night, leaving their belongings untouched but curiously covered in moths.
Here, the Balemurk spits and boils, the oppressive darkness pierced by scorching spears of fire.
They say if someone lies down to sleep beneath the trees, in the morning nothing will remain but a few scattered bones and a bed of blood-red lilies.
They say those who lose their way in the fields gradually wither and grow brittle, until at last they put down roots and anchor into the soil as a whispering stalk.
Here, the Mistmoors slump like a grieving parent, the once-thriving fields drowned by the relentless deluge.
Here, the Floodpits languish like a corpse, the clear waters choked by the filthy hands of the bog.
Here, the Hauntwoods churn like a viper's nest, as monstrous creatures prowl hungrily toward the ghostly light.
They say that if you stay in the cabin until the mists reach it, something will slither from the water and knock at the door.
They say dripping, hungry things writhe beyond the edge of the light, waiting to drag the unwary into the darkness.
They say every family who resided there met a grisly end, and once in a while you'll hear their screams echoing through the moldering halls.
They say its beckoning beacon leads not to safe harbor but into the arms of the drowned.
They say that those who enter the amusement park never come back, and their disembodied laughter joins the others on the wind.
They say the blades wait to bite through your skin until you've climbed too far to turn back, leaving you to cling with blood-slick hands until gravity takes you.
They say that with each new moon, the buried dead rise and dance from dusk to dawn, and witnesses to the revelry must join them for eternity.
The House's geography constantly warps and twists, fields melting into floorboards and walls opening into hungry maws.
Here, the Boilerbilges twitch like a trapped animal, peaks straining against the grasping roots and vines.
It is the one chamber whose location never changes, the rotten, rancorous heart of Duskmourn itself.
"A void rod? Perfect! Now I'll be able to get the glitch reader working again."
"The readings are off the charts! Whatever it is, it's close."

"See?! That's why you always burn the bodies."
—Rip, spawn hunter
Dance to its beat, or it will dance on your grave.
"I don't know what it was! Why would I stick around to find out?"
She's got a heart of gold, a nose for danger, and jaws that can pulverize a cellarspawn with a single snap.
"Huh, the detector won't stop beeping. Must be on the fritz again."

"Whatever happens, we need to stick togeth—AAAAGGGHHH!"
—Recovered tape fragment

"not dead just gone
IT WILL COME BACK"
—Note scrawled on a scrap of paper

"Rachel, it's me! I've . . . I've brought you back. We can finally be together. R-Rachel? Rach—"
—Recovered tape fragment

"DO NOT OPEN. Not a door."
—Bloodstained note

"Where do they keep coming [unintelligble screaming]"
—Recorded tape fragment
Here, the Balemurk spits and boils, the oppressive darkness pierced by scorching spears of fire.
Here, the Mistmoors slump like a grieving parent, the once-thriving fields drowned by the relentless deluge.
Here, the Floodpits languish like a corpse, the clear waters choked by the filthy hands of the bog.
Here, the Hauntwoods churn like a viper's nest, as monstrous creatures prowl hungrily toward the ghostly light.
Here, the Boilerbilges twitch like a trapped animal, peaks straining against the grasping roots and vines.
Vicky was so tired. The pain began to fade. "You were so brave," said her grandmother's voice from somewhere far away. "But it's time to rest now."
Cracks in the facade of the House lead not to escape but to oblivion.
Life thrives in the Hauntwoods, but it follows its own laws, unbound from the natural order.
With a flick of their wrist, Niko shattered the wickerfolk and whisked Nashi to safety.
"Give me a bit of steel and I'll deliver it into the hearts of my enemies."
A single light unleashes a hail of cleansing.
"Bend with the storm, then reply in kind."
The strongest of the pride are measured not by the steel in their hands but by the steel in their souls.
Her instinct is as sharp as her blade.
As the nim storm across the plains, a lone priest stands in their path. At his silent gesture, the battle line breaks, and the tide turns.
The Auriok have fought the metal hordes for so long now that knowing how to cripple them has become an instinct.
Defending to the death isn't always enough.
Before religion or civilization, there was order.
For the first and last time, the horrific creature experienced terror.
Leonin raising ceremonies take place at the white sun's dawn, the rebirth of artifacts mirroring the birth of a new day.

"I have seen the end of times, a future in which all our kind are torn from this world."
—Ushanti, leonin shaman
Theirs is a craft brought about by necessity, now raised to the level of art.
Those who survive the test bear a mark of power anyone can recognize.
"Your arrogance is my best weapon."
Stealing goblin weapons would be easier if the goblins were smart enough to let go.
A single lie unleashes a tide of disbelief.
It could be made to run silently, but its low hum reminds the Neurok that they are always watched.
"Someday, someone will best me. But it won't be today, and it won't be you."
As long as there are questions to be asked, the vedalken will ask them.
After the researcher's astonishing success, his assistants spent six hours finding a way to return the specimens safely to the ground.
"Why should I be bound by rules when I can see so far beyond them?"
Before labs or lectures, there was insight.

"Today's paperweight, tomorrow's leveler."
—Bruenna, Neurok leader

"Secrets are meant to remain secret."
—Memnarch
Memnarch shared a touch of his power with the vedalken in return for their service. It is a debt he intends to collect.
Art is unknown to the vedalken—for them, all creations must serve a purpose.

"The druids would be better off if they spent more time in the lab and less time watching trees grow."
—Pontifex, elder researcher

"May you wake to find you were only ever a dream."
—Mephidross curse

"The one who dies with the most toys is still dead."
—Geth, keeper of the Vault
Bottom feeders sometimes rise to the top.
The swarm's million wings stir the foulest of breezes.
A single fear unleashes a torrent of nightmares.
Mephidross claims all life within it. What cannot be twisted is absorbed.
Even on a world of metal, there are those who thirst for blood.
Their pain is so great, they can't help but share it with others.
In Mephidross, refuse doesn't last long—it's all scavenged, reanimated, or consumed.
Scavengers are always the first to pay their respects.
It is one of the oldest nim, steeped so long in the Dross that it has lost all vestiges of humanity.
Before tyrants or torturers, there was evil.
The beetles feed not on the flesh of corpses but on the metal, grinding out the iron and steel to add to their own bulky shells.
There's no escaping an enemy that lives inside your head.
When leonin settlers abandon their homes to the nim, items of value are often left behind.
Every creature on Mirrodin is a lightning rod.
Because fighting is easier than figuring out what else to do.

"If only the living were so easily salvaged."
—Memnarch

"Is it the stomping kind or the munching kind?"
—Slobad, goblin tinkerer
A single misstep unleashes an avalanche of ruin.
The spell fell upon the crowd like a dragon, ancient and full of death.

"Now I'm thirsty."
—Korva, Vulshok battlemaster
Always easily impressed, Durg was about to be blown away.
A Vulshok weapon strikes with the fire of the forge that made it.
Fallen enemies are fed to the scavengers. Fallen friends are thrown into the Great Furnace, their souls returned to the Great Mother.
Before wars or weapons, there was anger.
"You might want to work on your aim."

"I used to joke that he had been exiled for being too smart. Now I know why he never laughed."
—Glissa Sunseeker
Compared to the fire of the forge, the strength of steel is nothing.
It must eat its weight in metal daily, or its furnacelike belly will consume itself for lack of fuel.
Tel-Jilad's sworn protectors are the trolls, yet more fearsome protectors were created by the Tangle itself.
A single seed unleashes a flurry of growth.
In the Tangle, bad is often followed by worse.
Gelfruit grows abundantly wherever Sylvok druids live, as if the Tangle knows that humans are not as hardy as the beasts or as nimble as the elves.

"Ashes to ashes, rust to rust."
—Viridian shaman
Before predators or prey, there was life.
From the Radix at the hub of the Tangle all the way out to the Edges of Forgetting, a Viridian elf's life is built around the temporary.
Wurms compete for nesting grounds near the Radix. The young who hatch closest have the best chance for survival.
Strange times make for strange allies.
They're considered good luck by the elves they don't eat.
In bringing life to Mirrodin, Memnarch was more successful than he knew—for Mirrodin began to take on a life of its own.
"When the levelers come again, we shall be ready for them."
Thanks to the wolves, Tel-Jilad is the one area of Mirrodin the myr don't see often.
"We have no sun to guide our dead, so I tend the prismatic flames of the spirit fires that show the souls their way. When I die, I hope there is one left to guide my spirit home."
"I will fight only the way nature intended—and nature intended us to win."
If taken, it cuts the hand that clutches it. If given, it heals the hand that holds it.
It breaches not physical distances but temporal ones.
Break in case of emergency.
The parts are as strong as the whole.
Everything in its path is either pushed aside or ground under.
It converts the faintest surges of power from Mirrodin's core into usable energy, providing endless power for Memnarch's creations on the surface.

"Did it have this shape upon Mirrodin's creation, or did some inconceivable force shape the unshapable?"
—Pontifex, elder researcher
The ultimate treasure is one that guards itself.
Its curve mimics the twists of life and death.
Though no longer attached to the hand, it still holds its adversary in its grasp.
In close proximity, their magnetic energies merge and form a field of protection.
The longer it skulks through the corrosive gases of Mephidross, the more it adopts their thirst for death.
When Mirrodin's varied civilizations developed ways to fight the levelers, Memnarch upped the stakes.

"As the experimental population grows, so do the number of myr. It's a perfect equilibrium."
—Memnarch
The book shrieks horribly until its cover is opened, granting the spirit inside a moment's rest from the painful stirrings of the book's contents.
The goblins built it far larger than the cave opening, but to their glee, it smashed into the mountainside, ripping itself a new exit.
Bright as a mirror, dark as the sea.
In the blur between metal and flesh, Memnarch found madness.
One thing the myr can't do is enjoy the scenery.
Memnarch created the myr with three qualities in mind: dependability, controllability, and disposability.
The longer it patrols the smoldering crags of the Oxidda Chain, the more it adopts their fiery temper.
The longer it stands among the deadly blades of the Razor Fields, the more it adopts their harsh exterior.
It rolls with the punches.
The longer it soars above the shimmering swirls of the Quicksilver Sea, the more it adopts their unpredictability.
The longer it weaves through the twisted vines of the Tangle, the more it adopts their hidden strength.
It still stares accusingly at Memnarch, though millennia have passed since he separated the eye from its body.
The undead may outlast the living, but those who have never lived outlast them both.
It gives legs to the earth and wings to the sky.
Some say the knowledge lost during the Ritual of Rebuking is returned through the well's waters.

"The lifespan of a wirefly can be precisely described as 'short.'"
—Bruenna, Neurok leader
A wurm knows nothing of deception. If it opens its mouth, it plans to eat you.
Panopticon, forge of the Darksteel Eye, home of Mirrodin's keeper.
For hundreds of years Ugin slept, encased in the cocoon of stone and magic Sarkhan had created using a shard of a Zendikari hedron. As Ugin lay dormant, his spectral guardians kept vigil.
Martyred for worshipping her ancestors, she now walks among them.
"I would gladly give my life if it would inspire my clan to victory."
The aven are admired, for they are able to fly with the dragons.

"There is elegance in all the Ojutai do—even their killing."
—Kirada, Silumgar enforcer
"The blood of Dromoka and the blood of my veins are the same."
"Dromoka has taught me the secrets of her kind, that I might use them in her service."
Even the humblest guard of Ojutai's strongholds ponders the puzzles of the Great Teacher's lessons.
"We fight not out of fear, but for honor."
"The dragonlords rule the tempests of the skies. Here in the wastes, the storms are mine to command."
Dromoka has regard for the humans who serve under her. In return for her protection, they obey with steadfast loyalty, acting as weapons for her and her scalelords against the other clans.
Even after Anafenza was executed, many secretly maintained their beliefs in the old ways.

"My dragonlord is immortal. Most dragons are not."
—Kadri, Dromoka warrior
When Sarkhan saved Ugin in Tarkir's past, it changed Tarkir's future. The Sultai no longer exist, having been supplanted by the dragonlord Silumgar and his clan.

"Can you catch a snowflake on the edge of your blade? Her sword has snagged an entire blizzard."
—Zogye, Ojutai mystic
The trumpeters of Arashin are ever alert in their watch over the Great Aerie.

"The greatest gift Dromoka gives is the ability to fly without wings."
—Urdnan, Dromoka warrior
It heralded Sarkhan's return to Tarkir's present.

"If I fight, I might step on a butterfly. That would be sad."
—Krowg of Qal Sisma
The Shifting Wastes are Dromoka's domain. She will not tolerate intruders.

"If the scalelords are the brains of Dromoka's army, the supply caravans are its beating heart."
—Baihir, Dromoka mage
With heat, sand can form a delicate work of art; with pressure, an impenetrable bulwark.

"May our foes choke upon its horns!"
—Urdnan, Dromoka warrior

"Your bravery honors us all."
—Dromoka, translated from Draconic

"The Shifting Wastes provide our clan eternal protection. It is our duty to return the favor."
—Kadri, Dromoka warrior
Better scarves than scars.

"His companions are wise to follow him, for his foes dare not stand in his way."
—Zhiada, Dirgur protector
"Human enlightenment is a firefly that sparks in the night. Dragon enlightenment is a beacon that disperses all darkness."

"We trust in the scalelords, bringers of justice that none can escape."
—Urdnan, Dromoka warrior
Though she stood alone, she struck with the force of an army.

"Such lesser creatures must be purged from the sky. What use do they have but to help channel the lightning of our mighty dragonlord?"
—Gvar Barzeel, Kolaghan warrior

"Why eat now what could one day grow into a feast?"
—Ojutai, translated from Draconic
"When I have meditated on all outcomes, my opponent has no recourse."
Their lust for battle was so great that they didn't care their enemies wore their own faces.
Those who question Ojutai may not like the answers they receive.
The Ojutai believe in the Great Wheel: those who best serve the dragonlord are destined to be reborn as dragons.

"Learn to see an obstacle from a new perspective. Underneath, for example."
—Chanyi, Ojutai monk
Rakshasa waste no opportunity to display their wealth and power, even in the midst of a sorcerous duel.
The small are mostly ignored by dragons.
